public_payload.normalized_proposition: So-called agentic AI, supposedly powerful and autonomous, is actually incredibly demanding of its human users, who must set it up in many ways, connect it to many services, and check that every agent is instructed correctly, and its agents will cause problems with each other.

statement.excerpt: The so-called “agentic AI” that is supposedly powerful and autonomous is actually incredibly demanding of its human users — you must set it up in so many different ways and connect it to so many different services and check that every “agent” (different chatbot) is instructed in exactly the right way, and that none of these agents cause any problems (they will) with each other.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that substantial configuration and supervision are generally required of users of agentic workflows, especially the multi-agent workflows discussed in context.
Coordination failures are presented as an expected operational problem, not necessarily something that happens on every run.
Because no observation period is specified, use January–March 2026, the latest completed quarter before publication.
Distinguish work done by a product's developers from setup required of its end users.
criteria.support_condition: Representative workflow documentation and evaluations show substantial required user configuration, service integration, agent-specific instructions and supervision, alongside actual coordination failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that ordinary users generally achieve the relevant workflows without those burdens, or that the asserted coordination problems are not characteristic of them.
